notes: The author defines the mixed fundamental group through pairs consisting of an element of Gamma and a homotopy class of paths from P to its inverse-translated image. He writes a product with an interlinear Gamma component and explains his convention of composing paths like functions so that the fundamental groupoid acts on the left on étale-cover fibres. These are statements of the manuscript, not independently checked claims.

The second part chooses three elements over dotted symmetries, describes paths via semicircles and fixed-point loci, then introduces direct-oriented loops. The author writes relation(1), rejects the opposite displayed ordering, and supplies an inverse-product expression. The doubtful prime-like tick is left in relation(1), without using the later expression to erase it.

The top handwritten number is7 and the lower-left number is16; no date is written. A looped mark after the exclamation point may be an authorial question mark and remains unsure. The plainly repeated des in suivant des des quarts is retained as an authorial repetition.

Each C deletion was explicitly checked: initial correspondent/comprenant word; l’unique; stable par ... la symétrie; tau-sigma_i; and Au. Each C insertion was explicitly checked: gamma gamma-prime, U-prime, lambda_i, celui des, ens. des pts fixes, and (pour1∈Gamma). The uncertain cancelled words were not certified clear merely because their context suggested a reading.

Read page.jpg once for layout and both supplied native halves once line by line. Twenty-five saved enlarged crops cover all lexical differences, resolved C doubts, and newly opened places. Some contextual upper tips are clipped in crops10,13,18,23; the prescribed native-half reading supplied those strokes, and the later blind-reading boxes extend to contain the full selected inscriptions. No second first-reading crop of a decided place was made. Crop25 addresses only the newly noticed preceding-line suivant des, complementary to crop20.

The first page reader used no external research, OCR, other-page comparison, TeX compilation, proof check, or mathematical computation. Root independently reviewed all25 saved crops and agreed on retaining the local uncertainties and the repeated des. Remaining disagreements are reported from ink rather than repaired to expected mathematics.

Main-reader targeted check of the mixed fundamental-group product: if l goes from P to gamma^{-1}P and l-prime from P to gamma-prime^{-1}P, then gamma-prime^{-1}(l) after l-prime goes from P to gamma-prime^{-1}gamma^{-1}P=(gamma gamma-prime)^{-1}P. For a third pair (gamma-double-prime,l-double-prime), both associations have first component gamma gamma-prime gamma-double-prime and path gamma-double-prime^{-1}gamma-prime^{-1}(l) composed with gamma-double-prime^{-1}(l-prime) composed with l-double-prime. Thus the written multiplication is type-correct and associative on path classes under the stated left action and composition convention. This calculation does not decide whether the first handwritten path glyph is l or lambda, or prove the later geometric orientations.

The blind audit confirms the readable inserted ens. des pts fixes and lambda_i, the visible pas on the next baseline, the low bullet under l, and the repeated des des. It removes a comma supplied after the a_j,a_k parenthesis. The slash/parenthesis after path l, two à/colon forms, a crossed à/dotted-tau sign, au/à un/à segmentation, ne/un/en and the looped sign after ! remain qualified. The last sign may be a closing brace, so its interpretation as an authorial question is not asserted. These changes do not alter or extend the previously recorded type/associativity check of the product.
